name: Cappuccino
description: Espresso under a deep, airy cap of foam — lighter on milk and bolder than a latte.

steps.text: Pull a double espresso into a 150–180 ml cup.
Steam or froth the milk to about 60–65 °C, letting in plenty of air for a thick foam (roughly 2 cm).
Tap and swirl the pitcher to smooth the foam, then pour it into the espresso, finishing with a dome of foam.
Dust with cocoa if you like.

tips: Think of it as roughly equal thirds: espresso, milk, foam.

sources.name: Trade Coffee — Latte vs cappuccino vs flat white

name: Caffè Latte
description: A double espresso in a big cup of silky steamed milk with a thin layer of foam.

steps.text: Pull a double espresso into a 300–350 ml cup or glass.
Steam the milk to 60–65 °C, adding only a little air so it turns glossy, like wet paint.
Swirl the pitcher, then pour steadily into the centre of the espresso, finishing with a thin (about 1 cm) layer of foam.

tips: Any milk works. Oat milk steams best among the plant milks.

sources.name: Arla — Flat white vs latte vs cappuccino
Mug Cult — Latte, cappuccino, flat white guide

name: Flat White
description: A smaller, stronger-tasting latte: double espresso and velvety microfoam with barely any froth.

steps.text: Pull a double espresso (a ristretto-style double is traditional) into a 150–180 ml cup.
Steam the milk with only a brief burst of air, so you get tiny, glossy bubbles.
Pour low and steady so the microfoam folds into the crema, leaving a thin (around 5 mm) surface.

sources.name: Achilles Coffee Roasters — Cappuccino, flat white & latte

name: Cortado
description: Espresso 'cut' with an equal amount of warm milk. Smooth, balanced and small.

steps.text: Pull a double espresso into a small glass (around 120 ml).
Warm the milk with very little foam.
Pour roughly the same volume of milk as espresso and serve.

sources.name: Bean Box — Flat white vs latte vs cortado vs macchiato

name: Espresso Macchiato
description: Espresso 'stained' with a spoonful of milk foam — the smallest of the milk drinks.

steps.text: Pull a single or double espresso into a demitasse.
Froth a small amount of milk.
Spoon a dollop of foam onto the centre of the crema and serve.

tips: Not the same as a caramel macchiato, which is really a layered vanilla latte.

name: Latte Macchiato
description: Milk 'stained' by espresso: frothed milk in a tall glass with a shot poured through for pretty layers.

steps.text: Froth the milk generously and pour it into a tall glass. Let it sit for 30 seconds so the foam separates.
Pull a single espresso.
Pour the espresso slowly through the foam; it will settle as a band between milk and froth.

sources.name: Pro Coffee Gear — Coffee drinks chart

name: Caffè Mocha
description: A latte with chocolate stirred through: hot chocolate and espresso in one cup.

steps.text: Put the chocolate sauce in a mug and pull a double espresso on top of it.
Stir until the chocolate has completely dissolved.
Steam the milk and pour it in, then add whipped cream if you want to go all out.

tips: No sauce? Whisk 1 tbsp cocoa and 1 tbsp sugar into the hot espresso.

name: Café au Lait
description: Strong brewed coffee and hot milk in equal parts. No espresso machine needed.

steps.text: Brew about 150 ml of strong coffee in a French press, drip machine or pour-over.
Heat the milk in a small pan until steaming, but don't let it boil.
Pour coffee and milk into a wide cup or bowl at the same time, in roughly equal amounts.

tips: In France it's often served in a bowl for dunking bread.

sources.name: Canal Coffee Company — What is a café au lait?

name: Caffè Breve
description: An extra-rich American latte made with steamed half-and-half instead of milk.

steps.text: Pull a double espresso into a small cup.
Steam the half-and-half to 60–70 °C. It foams quickly and gets very thick.
Pour it over the espresso and serve.

name: Piccolo Latte
description: A tiny latte in a small glass: a ristretto shot topped with warm, lightly textured milk.

steps.text: Pull a ristretto (about 25 g) into a 90–120 ml glass.
Steam the milk with a little air for a thin layer of microfoam.
Top up the glass with milk and serve.
